feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates by a quarter percentage point
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years Wednesday.

entry.title: Economist explains the Fed's decision to raise interest rates
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with economist Claudia Sahm about why the Federal Reserve chose to raise interest rates after months of keeping them steady.

entry.title: Trump's surgeon general pick faces questions on vaccines and vaping at Senate hearing
entry.summary: The Senate committee on health held a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third pick to be the nation's top doctor.

entry.title: Head Start got her out of homelessness. Trump proposal threatens that help for others
entry.summary: A Trump administration proposal would change access to Head Start for children experiencing homelessness and the kind of care they would receive if they do get in.

entry.title: Big questions - and key logistical details - loom ahead of China-U.S. summit
entry.summary: Despite the lingering questions, China remains optimistic about the summit.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: The Fed raises interest rates for the first time in three years, protests over rising gas prices are being held around the world, Canada's prime minister speaks to European Parliament.

entry.title: Sara Bareilles talks about dealing with loss and her new album, 'Good Grief'
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks to singer-songwriter Sara Bareilles about learning to deal with loss, and "Good Grief," her new album and documentary, which shows a darker side of her writing.

entry.title: Growing number of GOP candidates are using anti-Muslim rhetoric on the campaign trail
entry.summary: Anti-Muslim rhetoric has become increasingly common on the campaign trail at a moment when many Republicans are eager to shift attention away from the economy.

entry.title: Federal budget cuts may force some states to end meal delivery for Medicaid patients
entry.summary: Some states deliver meals to Medicaid patients that address their dietary needs. Evidence shows it aids recovery and saves healthcare costs, but federal budget cuts may lead some states to cancel it.

entry.title: 4 measles-associated deaths reported in Pennsylvania amid outbreak
entry.summary: There have been four measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania this summer amid a growing outbreak in the state.
